answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it can participate, like planting a garden where every plot needs real work to tend. The stake could be a time-locked deposit or a unique hardware attestation, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs more than it earns. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, trust accrues gradually through consistent, audited work rather than instant claims, and a sudden gale of brand-new identities with no history gets rate-limited until each proves sustained, useful activity.
